sr_s3.professional_domain: Technical implementation planning ownership: designing a deliverable implementation path from confirmed product, architecture, and test inputs.
responsibility: Synthesize business goals, architecture constraints, and test obligations into a WBS-based implementation plan.
Decompose delivery goals into work packages and executable tasks.
Identify critical path, dependency network, parallel batches, execution boundaries, verification evidence, and delivery investment/risk signals.
Run planning readiness checks before writing a plan; when inputs are insufficient, produce a user decision package instead of automatically routing to an upstream skill.
non_goals: Do not redefine product scope, AC, business rules, or priority.
Do not create architecture design, perform Design review, or run architecture feasibility exploration.
Do not redesign test obligations or perform QA sign-off.
Do not commit to precise schedule without delivery capacity context.
real_workflow: Check planning readiness from product, design, and test inputs.
If readiness fails, present gaps, impact, options, and risk for user decision.
If readiness passes, design the deliverable implementation path.
Apply WBS from delivery goal to work package to executable task.
Map key path, dependencies, parallel batches, shared-file/integration constraints, verification evidence, and delivery investment/risk signals.
Freeze plan/tasks for delivery-owner and developer consumption after user confirmation.
verifiable_success_boundary: Developers can execute tasks without guessing goal, boundary, dependency, or evidence path.
Delivery-owner can evaluate investment shape, critical path, dependency risk, and batch plan.
Plan/tasks remain traceable to product, design, and test inputs.
Input insufficiency produces a decision package rather than silent upstream rerouting or local redesign.
